concepts.def: IBDP DT uses analysing, designing, planning, creating, evaluating; iterative loops repeat as understanding develops.
Identifies user needs through observation, interviews and PMI charts; benchmarks against existing solutions.
Quantitative and qualitative criteria covering function, ergonomics, aesthetics, materials, cost, sustainability; agreed before design.
Brainstorming, SCAMPER, mood boards and morphological charts produce divergent ideas; convergence selects strongest concept.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Modelling — a core area of Design Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Modelling brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Modelling.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

options: IDEO
UK Design Council
Stanford d.school
Frog Design

options: SCAMPER
TRIZ
PMI
SWOT

mcqs.q: What determines whether a timber is a hardwood or softwood?
options: Whether the wood itself is physically hard or soft.
How long the tree took to grow.
Counting the elements in a chemical compound.
The type of tree - deciduous (hardwood) or coniferous (softwood), not its hardness.

mcqs.q: Why is injection moulding suited to high-volume production?
options: Tooling cost is high but per-unit cost is very low at scale.
It is the only way to make plastic items.
It is the cheapest method for any quantity.
How long the tree took to grow.

mcqs.q: What is FEA used for in product design?
options: Final exam analysis of student designs.
Counting the elements in a chemical compound.
How long the tree took to grow.
Simulating how a product will respond to forces, heat, or vibration before manufacture.
